answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks via ultra-wideband two-way ranging backed by fixed anchor beacons. When a field agent registers near a canyon, dune, or river, anchors issue nonces and time signed replies to multilaterate its location. Because co-located keys violate a minimum-separation rule and RF propagation resists remote spoofing, an attacker must buy, power, and disperse UWB transceivers per identity. However, multipath reflections can skew distance estimates and exclude honest agents.
